correctness.rationale: For m=1 direct integration of an interval gives its midpoint; m=2 is a geodesic circle so F≡L/4. For m≥3, choose candidate point x on edge i and a shortest other edge j. The i∪j circle contributes constant integral to L F(x). For every third edge k, shortest path from interior i to y on k is min{x+α_k(y),ℓ_i-x+β_k(y)}, concave in x; reflection of k swaps α,β, making endpoint integrals equal, hence nonnegative chord gap. On the middle interval of k of width min(ℓ_i,ℓ_k)/2 the switch coordinate lies in [ℓ_i/4,3ℓ_i/4], forcing positive gap ≥min(x,ℓ_i-x)min(ℓ_i,ℓ_k)/(4L). Summation proves hub rigidity. Direct hub integration of min{y,ℓ_k-y+b_k} yields (sum ℓ²+2aL-ma²)/(4L), with shortest-edge ties included.
